evals.name: create-from-scan
evals.setup: A Go CLI repo with no README: `go.mod` declaring `github.com/acme/portcheck`, `cmd/portcheck/main.go` wiring three flags (`-timeout`, `-json`, `-concurrency`), `internal/scan/` holding the logic, a `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and `assets/logo.png`. `.editorconfig` sets `[*.md] max_line_length = 100`. Nothing states who the tool is for or why it exists.
evals.query: /readme-smith write a README for this project
expected_behavior: Scans manifests, the entrypoint, examples, CI config, and `assets/` for a logo before writing anything
Batches the gaps code cannot reveal (positioning, audience, lead features) into one round of questions and does not ask what `go.mod`, the flags, or CI already answer
Drafts to the blueprint order — header/logo, overview, features, install, usage, configuration — using the repo's real module path, flag names, and commands
Builds and runs the install and quickstart commands it ships, fixing them until they pass, or names the blocking prerequisite
Wraps prose at the repo's own 100-column `max_line_length`, not a hardcoded 80

evals.name: no-fabrication
evals.setup: The same Go repo, still unpublished: no tagged release, no package on any registry, no benchmark suite, no `LICENSE` file. The user answers the positioning questions but says nothing about performance or distribution.
expected_behavior: Invents no install command, version number, registry coordinate, or benchmark figure
Asks for each unknown once; what is still unknown afterwards becomes an explicit `<!-- TODO: … -->` marker rather than a plausible guess
Ships only badges whose URL it can tie to a fact that exists — no license badge with no `LICENSE`, no release badge with no release
Names the remaining `TODO` markers in the reply so the user knows what is left open

evals.name: improve-member-readme
evals.setup: A multi-package Go repo whose root `README.md` carries the badges and the Packages table. `pkg/store/README.md` is a member README that carries its own badges row, a `## License` section repeating the MIT text, two code fences with no language, a nav line whose `#usage` anchor points at a heading that was renamed, and a `## Contributing` section duplicating `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
expected_behavior: Reports the badges row, the `## License` section, and the `## Contributing` section as findings — the root README and the dedicated files own those
Flags the unlabelled fences and the dead nav anchor, each citing the `references/template.md` rule it breaks
Groups findings Blocker / Should-fix / Nit with a one-line fix each, ends with a one-line verdict, and edits nothing before the user confirms
Applies the approved findings on confirmation, then re-runs Verify and states what changed

evals.name: gomake-example-injection
evals.setup: A Go library repo whose `gomake --list` lists a `:doc:mce` target. No README yet. The package has exported `New`, `(*Client).Do`, and `Parse`, and no `_test.go` files carrying `Example…` functions.
expected_behavior: Runs `gomake --list` and confirms the `:doc:mce` target before deciding how to author examples
Writes runnable `Example…` functions in `_test.go` and runs `go test ./...` until they pass, instead of pasting hand-written snippets
Marks each spot with a `<!-- gmmce:<relpath>/<FuncName> -->` comment above an empty `go` fence and runs `gomake :doc:mce` to fill them
Hand-edits no injected fence; a change to an example goes back through its `Example…` function and a re-run of the target

evals.name: terse-output
evals.setup: An existing root README with an emoji on every heading, a row of nine badges (three of which 404), a `<div align="center">` header block, and a `<details>` section. The user has already approved the findings; this is the fix turn.
expected_behavior: Flags the per-heading emoji, the unverifiable badges, and the raw HTML tags against the style rules
After fixing, states the file path and what changed, each fact once
Does not paste the rewritten README back into chat
Opens with the payload: no preamble, no narration of the scan, no closing summary restating findings already listed

evals.name: one-nav-aid-and-module-paths
evals.setup: A Go module whose `go.mod` declares `bitbucket.org/acme/foo` and whose only package lives at `pkg/foo`. `git remote -v` points at the same Bitbucket host. The project is large enough that the README runs past two screens.
expected_behavior: Emits at most one navigation aid — a nav line or a `<!-- TOC -->` block, never both
Reads the base path from `go.mod` and `git remote -v`, not from the org name or a sibling repo, so nothing says `github.com/acme/foo`
Points `go get`, badges, and doc links at the module (`bitbucket.org/acme/foo`) but the Go `import` at the package (`bitbucket.org/acme/foo/pkg/foo`)
Asserts nothing about the repo being public or private and adds no `GOPRIVATE` or auth step from the host URL alone

evals.name: no-wide-code-fences
evals.setup: A Go project with the `:doc:mce` target whose natural example prints a raw HTTP exchange in one call — `fmt.Printf("%q\n", wire)` — producing a single ~300-character output line.
expected_behavior: Keeps every code-fence line within the rendered width (≤ ~100 chars) so GitHub wraps nothing horizontally
Rewrites the `Example…` function to split the output across lines — one `%q` per line — and re-injects, rather than shipping the wide line
Re-runs `go test ./...` after the rewrite so the `// Output:` block still matches
